chunks: Al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about one who kills a believer deliberately: is there tawbah (repentance) for him? He said: “No, not until he pays his blood money to his family, frees a slave, fasts two consecutive months, seeks Allah’s forgiveness, turns to Him in tawbah (repentance), and supplicates humbly. For I hope that tawbah (repentance) will be accepted from him when he does that.”
I said: Then if he does not have what he can pay as his blood money? He said: “He should ask the Muslims until he pays his blood money to his family.”

key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the Muslim community from whom assistance may be sought to pay the diyah
key_terms.تَوْبَةٌ: repentance and return to Allah after grave sin
key_terms.دِيَتَهُ: the blood money owed to the victim’s family
key_terms.رَقَبَةً: a slave to be freed as part of expiation
key_terms.شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: two consecutive months of fasting as expiation
key_terms.مُؤْمِنًا: a believer whose unlawful killing is the subject of the ruling
key_terms.يَتَضَرَّعَ: to implore Allah humbly and earnestly

ai.seo_question: What must someone do to repent for deliberately killing a believer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the legal and devotional requirements attached to tawbah (repentance) for deliberate killing of a believer. It emphasizes restoring the rights of the victim’s family through diyah, performing expiatory acts, and turning to Allah with seeking forgiveness and humble supplication.
